Those heavy feelings of guilt and being a burden have hung over me almost the entire year.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand if there have been any notable changes in the intensity of these feelings over the past year, or have they remained relatively stable, and have you noticed any triggers that make them worse or better?\n\nPatient: These heavy feelings have stayed pretty constant, though last fall there was a brief time when the sadness lifted just enough that I could get through my shifts without crying. They definitely get worse with the stress of managing my home and finances all on my own, or when there's tension with my ex-spouse about family gatherings.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that these feelings have been almost constant for over a year, but can you tell me if you've had any episodes of significant depressive symptoms that lasted for at least two weeks but then improved, or have the symptoms been persistent without clear episodes of worsening and improvement?\n\nPatient: It’s really been a persistent, heavy feeling without any clear episodes of getting better and then worse again. Even though I know I am physically alone when I hear that man's voice, it sounds so clear and real that I can't help but believe it's actually happening rather than just being in my head.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to ignore the voice or question the reality of being watched - do the thoughts or voices get louder, softer, or do they change in any way?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if they change, to be honest. When it's happening, I just feel so overwhelmed by it all that I haven't really tried to challenge or ignore them in that way.\n\nDoctor: When you hear the voice or have these thoughts about being watched, are you able to recognize that they might not be based in reality, or do you firmly believe they are real and happening to you?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe they are real and actually happening to me. Even when I try to think about it logically, the conviction that the city is watching me and the sound of that man's voice behind my ear are just too powerful and undeniable to ignore.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times when you've had these thoughts or heard the voice and then later realized they weren't real or based on actual events, or do you always believe them to be true at the moment they're happening?\n\nPatient: In the moment, they always feel completely real and I absolutely believe them. I am entirely convinced that the school district is documenting my mistakes, and even when I logically know I'm alone in my apartment, that man's voice sounds too real not to believe the awful things he says.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and the thoughts about being watched relate to your feelings of guilt and being a burden, and do you think they are connected or separate issues?\n\nPatient: They feel deeply connected to me. When that man's voice is behind my ear telling me I'm useless, and I see people watching me at the crosswalk, it just confirms that I really am a burden who is letting everyone down. In fact, most days while I'm standing there feeling that heavy weight of guilt in my chest, I'm hearing the voice criticize me at the exact same time.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of unusual perceptions or beliefs, such as seeing things that aren't there or smelling odors that no one else can, in addition to the voice you hear and the feeling of being watched?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see things that aren't there, and I've never smelled any strange odors. My experiences are really just limited to hearing that man's voice behind my left ear and feeling like the parents and city people are constantly watching me and documenting my mistakes.\n\nDoctor: When you hear the voice telling you that you're useless, do you think it's a part of your own thoughts and feelings of guilt, or do you believe it's an external voice that's telling you something true about yourself?\n\nPatient: It feels like a real, physical voice of a man speaking from just behind my left ear, not like my own internal thoughts at all. And because I already feel so much guilt and like a failure, I believe what he's saying is the absolute truth, which just makes it so much more painful.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched are present even when you're not feeling particularly guilty or down, or if they seem to only occur when you're in a low mood?\n\nPatient: Yes, they still happen even when my mood is a bit better. Last fall, there was a spell where my sadness had eased and I wasn't crying during my shifts, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me and was sure the school district was secretly collecting evidence on me.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched seem to be directly related to your feelings of guilt and being a burden, or do they seem to be separate and unrelated to your mood?"

On my worst days at the crosswalk, I picture stepping off the curb in front of one of the trucks, and I have to grip the stop sign pole tightly just to keep myself from doing it. It really scares me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes where you heard voices or saw things that weren't there, or had thoughts that seemed very strange or unreal to you, during this time of feeling down and guilty?\n\nPatient: Yes, I have. Almost every week, I hear a man's voice right behind my left ear telling me I'm useless and that the kids would be safer if I wasn't there, even when I'm completely alone. At the same time, I've been convinced that parents and city workers are secretly watching me and documenting my mistakes at the crosswalk to prove I'm unfit to be around the children.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about the voice you hear and the beliefs about being watched, such as when they started, how often they occur, and if they seem to be triggered by anything in particular?\n\nPatient: They started about a year and a few months ago, and the voice comments on what I'm doing pretty much every week, even when I'm alone in my apartment. The feeling that parents and city officials are keeping tabs on me at the crosswalk is also constant, and it even continued last fall during that brief spell when my sadness had temporarily eased.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched are real, or do you think they might be a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: They feel completely real to me, and I am truly convinced that the parents and city officials are keeping tabs on me to document my mistakes. Even though I know I am physically alone when I hear that man's voice, it sounds so clear and real that I can't help but believe it's actually happening rather than just being in my head.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to ignore the voice or question the reality of being watched - do the thoughts or voices get louder, softer, or do they change in any way?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if they change, to be honest. When it's happening, I just feel so overwhelmed by it all that I haven't really tried to challenge or ignore them in that way.\n\nDoctor: When you hear the voice or have these thoughts about being watched, are you able to recognize that they might not be based in reality, or do you firmly believe they are real and happening to you?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe they are real and actually happening to me. Even when I try to think about it logically, the conviction that the city is watching me and the sound of that man's voice behind my ear are just too powerful and undeniable to ignore.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times when you've had these thoughts or heard the voice and then later realized they weren't real or based on actual events, or do you always believe them to be true at the moment they're happening?\n\nPatient: In the moment, they always feel completely real and I absolutely believe them. I am entirely convinced that the school district is documenting my mistakes, and even when I logically know I'm alone in my apartment, that man's voice sounds too real not to believe the awful things he says.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and the thoughts about being watched relate to your feelings of guilt and being a burden, and do you think they are connected or separate issues?\n\nPatient: They feel deeply connected to me. When that man's voice is behind my ear telling me I'm useless, and I see people watching me at the crosswalk, it just confirms that I really am a burden who is letting everyone down. In fact, most days while I'm standing there feeling that heavy weight of guilt in my chest, I'm hearing the voice criticize me at the exact same time.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of unusual perceptions or beliefs, such as seeing things that aren't there or smelling odors that no one else can, in addition to the voice you hear and the feeling of being watched?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see things that aren't there, and I've never smelled any strange odors. My experiences are really just limited to hearing that man's voice behind my left ear and feeling like the parents and city people are constantly watching me and documenting my mistakes.\n\nDoctor: When you hear the voice telling you that you're useless, do you think it's a part of your own thoughts and feelings of guilt, or do you believe it's an external voice that's telling you something true about yourself?\n\nPatient: It feels like a real, physical voice of a man speaking from just behind my left ear, not like my own internal thoughts at all. And because I already feel so much guilt and like a failure, I believe what he's saying is the absolute truth, which just makes it so much more painful.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched are present even when you're not feeling particularly guilty or down, or if they seem to only occur when you're in a low mood?\n\nPatient: Yes, they still happen even when my mood is a bit better. Last fall, there was a spell where my sadness had eased and I wasn't crying during my shifts, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me and was sure the school district was secretly collecting evidence on me.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched seem to be directly related to your feelings of guilt and being a burden, or do they seem to be separate and unrelated to your mood?\n\nPatient: They feel very connected because the voice says things that feed right into my guilt, like telling me I'm useless and the kids would be safer without me, and I often hear it at the exact same time I feel that heavy, hopeless mood. But they aren't entirely tied to my mood, because during that spell last fall when my sadness lifted a bit, I still heard the voice and felt like I was being watched.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are times when the voice you hear and the thoughts of being watched seem to be triggered by your feelings of guilt and being a burden, or if they occur independently of your mood?\n\nPatient: They really seem to occur independently of my mood. Even during that spell last fall when my sadness had eased slightly and I wasn't feeling as down, I still heard the man's voice criticizing me and remained convinced the school district was gathering evidence against me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched would stop or change if your feelings of guilt and being a burden went away, or do you think they would continue regardless of how you're feeling?"

Even when my daughter or church friends reach out, I just can't bring myself to care enough to respond.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever thought about harming yourself or had thoughts of not wanting to live anymore during this difficult time?\n\nPatient: Yes... for months now, I've caught myself thinking it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up. On my worst days at the crosswalk, I picture stepping off the curb in front of one of the trucks, and I have to grip the stop sign pole tightly just to keep myself from doing it. It really scares me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes where you heard voices or saw things that weren't there, or had thoughts that seemed very strange or unreal to you, during this time of feeling down and guilty?\n\nPatient: Yes, I have. Almost every week, I hear a man's voice right behind my left ear telling me I'm useless and that the kids would be safer if I wasn't there, even when I'm completely alone. At the same time, I've been convinced that parents and city workers are secretly watching me and documenting my mistakes at the crosswalk to prove I'm unfit to be around the children.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about the voice you hear and the beliefs about being watched, such as when they started, how often they occur, and if they seem to be triggered by anything in particular?\n\nPatient: They started about a year and a few months ago, and the voice comments on what I'm doing pretty much every week, even when I'm alone in my apartment. The feeling that parents and city officials are keeping tabs on me at the crosswalk is also constant, and it even continued last fall during that brief spell when my sadness had temporarily eased.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched are real, or do you think they might be a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: They feel completely real to me, and I am truly convinced that the parents and city officials are keeping tabs on me to document my mistakes. Even though I know I am physically alone when I hear that man's voice, it sounds so clear and real that I can't help but believe it's actually happening rather than just being in my head.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to ignore the voice or question the reality of being watched - do the thoughts or voices get louder, softer, or do they change in any way?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if they change, to be honest. When it's happening, I just feel so overwhelmed by it all that I haven't really tried to challenge or ignore them in that way.\n\nDoctor: When you hear the voice or have these thoughts about being watched, are you able to recognize that they might not be based in reality, or do you firmly believe they are real and happening to you?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe they are real and actually happening to me. Even when I try to think about it logically, the conviction that the city is watching me and the sound of that man's voice behind my ear are just too powerful and undeniable to ignore.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times when you've had these thoughts or heard the voice and then later realized they weren't real or based on actual events, or do you always believe them to be true at the moment they're happening?\n\nPatient: In the moment, they always feel completely real and I absolutely believe them. When that man's voice is behind my ear telling me I'm useless, and I see people watching me at the crosswalk, it just confirms that I really am a burden who is letting everyone down. Since then, they’ve been almost constant, hanging over me nearly the entire time, even during brief periods when some of my other struggles seemed to let up a bit.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods over the past year where you felt significantly better for at least a couple of months, or have these feelings of guilt and being a burden been relatively consistent without much improvement?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any long stretches like a couple of months where I felt significantly better. There was a brief spell last fall where the sadness lifted slightly and I could get through my shifts without crying, but it didn't last. Those heavy feelings of guilt and being a burden have hung over me almost the entire year.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand if there have been any notable changes in the intensity of these feelings over the past year, or have they remained relatively stable, and have you noticed any triggers that make them worse or better?\n\nPatient: These heavy feelings have stayed pretty constant, though last fall there was a brief time when the sadness lifted just enough that I could get through my shifts without crying. They definitely get worse with the stress of managing my home and finances all on my own, or when there's tension with my ex-spouse about family gatherings.\n\nDoctor: You've mentioned that these feelings have been almost constant for over a year, but can you tell me if you've had any episodes of significant depressive symptoms that lasted for at least two weeks but then improved, or have the symptoms been persistent without clear episodes of worsening and improvement?\n\nPatient: It’s really been a persistent, heavy feeling without any clear episodes of getting better and then worse again. I don't go to church events anymore, and when my daughter or friends reach out, I just stare at my phone because I can't bring myself to care enough to reply. Even when my daughter or church friends reach out, I just can't bring myself to care enough to respond.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever thought about harming yourself or had thoughts of not wanting to live anymore during this difficult time?\n\nPatient: Yes... for months now, I've caught myself thinking it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up. I just don't have it in me to join in on anything anymore.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any activities or things that still bring you some joy or pleasure, no matter how small, despite feeling this way?\n\nPatient: Honestly, no, there really isn't anything that brings me joy anymore. It feels like the light has gone out inside of me, and I'm just going through the motions under a constant gray cloud. Even when my daughter or church friends reach out, I just can't bring myself to care enough to respond.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever thought about harming yourself or had thoughts of not wanting to live anymore during this difficult time?\n\nPatient: Yes... for months now, I've caught myself thinking it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up. On my worst days at the crosswalk, I picture stepping off the curb in front of one of the trucks, and I have to grip the stop sign pole tightly just to keep myself from doing it. It really scares me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any episodes where you heard voices or saw things that weren't there, or had thoughts that seemed very strange or unreal to you, during this time of feeling down and guilty?\n\nPatient: Yes, I have. Almost every week, I hear a man's voice right behind my left ear telling me I'm useless and that the kids would be safer if I wasn't there, even when I'm completely alone. At the same time, I've been convinced that parents and city workers are secretly watching me and documenting my mistakes at the crosswalk to prove I'm unfit to be around the children.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe more about the voice you hear and the beliefs about being watched, such as when they started, how often they occur, and if they seem to be triggered by anything in particular?\n\nPatient: They started about a year and a few months ago, and the voice comments on what I'm doing pretty much every week, even when I'm alone in my apartment. The feeling that parents and city officials are keeping tabs on me at the crosswalk is also constant, and it even continued last fall during that brief spell when my sadness had temporarily eased.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched are real, or do you think they might be a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: They feel completely real to me, and I am truly convinced that the parents and city officials are keeping tabs on me to document my mistakes. Even though I know I am physically alone when I hear that man's voice, it sounds so clear and real that I can't help but believe it's actually happening rather than just being in my head.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to ignore the voice or question the reality of being watched - do the thoughts or voices get louder, softer, or do they change in any way?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if they change, to be honest. Even when I try to think about it logically, the conviction that the city is watching me and the sound of that man's voice behind my ear are just too powerful and undeniable to ignore.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times when you've had these thoughts or heard the voice and then later realized they weren't real or based on actual events, or do you always believe them to be true at the moment they're happening?\n\nPatient: In the moment, they always feel completely real and I absolutely believe them. I am entirely convinced that the school district is documenting my mistakes, and even when I logically know I'm alone in my apartment, that man's voice sounds too real not to believe the awful things he says.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and the thoughts about being watched relate to your feelings of guilt and being a burden, and do you think they are connected or separate issues?\n\nPatient: They feel deeply connected to me. My experiences are really just limited to hearing that man's voice behind my left ear and feeling like the parents and city people are constantly watching me and documenting my mistakes.\n\nDoctor: When you hear the voice telling you that you're useless, do you think it's a part of your own thoughts and feelings of guilt, or do you believe it's an external voice that's telling you something true about yourself?\n\nPatient: It feels like a real, physical voice of a man speaking from just behind my left ear, not like my own internal thoughts at all. And because I already feel so much guilt and like a failure, I believe what he's saying is the absolute truth, which just makes it so much more painful.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched are present even when you're not feeling particularly guilty or down, or if they seem to only occur when you're in a low mood?\n\nPatient: Yes, they still happen even when my mood is a bit better. Last fall, there was a spell where my sadness had eased and I wasn't crying during my shifts, but I still heard that man's voice criticizing me and was sure the school district was secretly collecting evidence on me.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched seem to be directly related to your feelings of guilt and being a burden, or do they seem to be separate and unrelated to your mood?\n\nPatient: They feel very connected because the voice says things that feed right into my guilt, like telling me I'm useless and the kids would be safer without me, and I often hear it at the exact same time I feel that heavy, hopeless mood. But they aren't entirely tied to my mood, because during that spell last fall when my sadness lifted a bit, I still heard the voice and felt like I was being watched.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are times when the voice you hear and the thoughts of being watched seem to be triggered by your feelings of guilt and being a burden, or if they occur independently of your mood?\n\nPatient: They really seem to occur independently of my mood. Even during that spell last fall when my sadness had eased slightly and I wasn't feeling as down, I still heard the man's voice criticizing me and remained convinced the school district was gathering evidence against me.\n\nDoctor: Do you think the voice you hear and the thoughts about being watched would stop or change if your feelings of guilt and being a burden went away, or do you think they would continue regardless of how you're feeling?\n\nPatient: I think they would continue regardless of how I'm feeling. Even last fall when my sadness eased a bit and I wasn't crying as much, I still heard that man's voice criticizing me and felt completely convinced the school district was secretly collecting evidence against me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a period where the voice stopped or significantly reduced for a while, and if so, what was happening in your life during that time?\n\nPatient: Yes, there was a brief spell last fall where the voice and the feeling of being watched let up a bit for a few weeks. Even though I know I am physically alone when I hear that man's voice, it sounds so clear and real that I can't help but believe it's actually happening rather than just being in my head.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to ignore the voice or question the reality of being watched - do the thoughts or voices get louder, softer, or do they change in any way?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure if they change, to be honest. When it's happening, I just feel so overwhelmed by it all that I haven't really tried to challenge or ignore them in that way.\n\nDoctor: When you hear the voice or have these thoughts about being watched, are you able to recognize that they might not be based in reality, or do you firmly believe they are real and happening to you?\n\nPatient: I firmly believe they are real and actually happening to me. Even when I try to think about it logically, the conviction that the city is watching me and the sound of that man's voice behind my ear are just too powerful and undeniable to ignore.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any times when you've had these thoughts or heard the voice and then later realized they weren't real or based on actual events, or do you always believe them to be true at the moment they're happening?\n\nPatient: In the moment, they always feel completely real and I absolutely believe them. I am entirely convinced that the school district is documenting my mistakes, and even when I logically know I'm alone in my apartment, that man's voice sounds too real not to believe the awful things he says.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how the voice and the thoughts about being watched relate to your feelings of guilt and being a burden, and do you think they are connected or separate issues?\n\nPatient: They feel deeply connected to me.
